occlusion.note:
WHICH FOREGROUND PLANE MASKS AN ACTOR STANDING IN EACH BAND. Tyler's ruling, and it is authored here rather than emitted by the compiler because occlusion geometry is a reading of the PICTURE and every room's is different. The compiler previously wrote `clipPlane: 12` into every box it made -- a constant that named no plane this room declares, so Renderer.masked() looked it up, found nothing, and drew straight through. Two masks loaded and occluded nobody, and no validator could see it because none of them asked whether the number on a box named a plane the room had. Doc 36 Q14.

THE ASSIGNMENT FOLLOWS THE PLANES' OWN NOTES. Plane 1 is the near corner alone -- the lumber stack and the wagon wheel -- so an actor in the near mud passes BEHIND that and IN FRONT of the trough. Plane 2 is plane 1 plus the hitching rail and the trough, so an actor in the middle band or further back is behind all of it. No box in this room is clipPlane 0: doc 22 defines 0 as always-in-front and nothing on Main Street is nearer than the wagon wheel, whose base sits on the bottom row of the frame.

BOTH PLANES ARE maskPending. The assignment above is Tyler's ruling and is what the room will use; the masks it points at were authored against an earlier, narrower Main Street and describe objects the current plate does not contain. The clip planes are right and the art is stale, and those are two different repairs.
occlusion.clipPlaneNote: BY BAND, NOT BY CARVED PIECE. The compiler cuts each band around the obstacles standing in it -- mud_far becomes three pieces around the trough -- and every piece of one band is at the same depth, so authoring a plane per piece would be authoring the same decision three times and inviting the three to disagree. A piece inherits its band's value; a band with no authored value is a build failure naming the band.

proofPoints.note: In the near mud where plane 1's mask, stretched to the room, covers x0-940 across the whole band. GEOMETRICALLY SOUND AND VISUALLY WRONG, which is why the plane is marked maskPending: what the mask draws there is a wagon wheel and the plate underneath is open mud. Kept, not deleted -- the day the mask is regenerated against this plate, the near band's proof point is already standing and the assertion goes live with it.

In the middle band where plane 2 adds coverage beyond plane 1's corner: a hitching rail, two posts and a crossbar, drawn precisely, and there is no hitching rail in the plate there. Same state as the near point and kept for the same reason. Errata 300: the street's bands now start at y666, so this point is in the far band; plane 2 for both, so nothing it proves changes.

planes.note: The near corner alone -- the lumber stack and the wagon wheel. An actor in the near mud is masked by this and by nothing else, so he passes BEHIND the woodpile and IN FRONT of the trough, which is the point of having two planes rather than one flat overlay.
planes.maskPendingIssue: docs/36-issue-list.md::Q20 · BOTH OF MAIN STREET'S OCCLUSION MASKS DESCRIBE A STREET THAT NO LONGER EXISTS
planes.maskPendingNote:
THE MASK DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS PLATE. Found by rendering it over the background and looking, which is the only way it could have been found: the shapes are well-formed, they sit in plausible places, and every geometric test passes on them -- check-occlusion measures 31% of the drawn figure covered at the proof point below, which is a real overlap with a shape that is not in the picture.

MEASURED. The mask is 320x144 -- errata 54's voided presentation, doc 36 Q17 -- and `Renderer.masked` stretches it to the room's 3700x864, which is a defined behaviour and not the same as authoring it at room resolution. Stretched, plane 1 draws a WAGON WHEEL with eight spokes and a slab beside it across x0-940 of the near mud. The plate there is open mud: no wheel, no lumber, nothing. Panel C of the room proof shows a man standing in the middle of it, drawn whole, with nothing to be behind.

I GOT THIS WRONG ONCE AND THE WAY I GOT IT WRONG IS THE WARNING. Reading the overlay, I took the wheel the MASK draws for a wheel in the PLATE and recorded that plane 1 'traces the wheel's spokes exactly'. It traces its own. A mask rendered over a background looks like a highlighted object whether or not there is an object there, and only turning the mask off answers it.

WHILE THIS IS TRUE THE RENDERER SKIPS THE PLANE and draws straight through -- which is what it did anyway when every box said clipPlane 12, so nothing regresses. Regenerating both masks at 3700x864 against the current plate is art, and Tyler's.

planes.note: Plane 1 plus the hitching rail and the water trough. CONTAINS plane 1 on purpose: doc 22 section 5 says an actor is masked by its own plane and not by a union of every plane, so each level has to carry everything nearer than the actors assigned to it. An actor in the middle band or further is behind all of it.
planes.maskPendingIssue: docs/36-issue-list.md::Q20 · BOTH OF MAIN STREET'S OCCLUSION MASKS DESCRIBE A STREET THAT NO LONGER EXISTS
planes.maskPendingNote:
THE MASK IS STALE AND DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS PLATE. Found by rendering it over the background and looking, which is the only way it could have been found: the shapes are well-formed, they are in plausible places, and every geometric test passes on them.

MEASURED. The mask is 320x144 -- errata 54's voided presentation, doc 36 Q17 -- and `Renderer.masked` stretches it to the room's 3700x864, which is a defined behaviour and not the same as authoring it at room resolution. Stretched, plane 2 adds two regions beyond plane 1's corner: x1110-1640 in the middle band, which is a HITCHING RAIL, two posts and a crossbar, drawn precisely -- and there is no hitching rail in the plate there; and x2480-2930, a plain rectangle over open mud in front of the saloon. Neither touches the water trough at x1862-2017 y543-605, which this plane's own note says it contains. It was authored against an earlier, narrower Main Street.

PLANE 1 IS PENDING FOR THE SAME REASON, and was nearly not: its mask draws a wagon wheel over what is open mud in the current plate, and the wheel looked like the plate's until the mask was turned off. Both masks are stale together.

WHILE THIS IS TRUE THE RENDERER SKIPS THE PLANE and draws straight through -- which is what it did anyway when every box said clipPlane 12, so nothing regresses. Activating a stale mask would be worse than the inert state it replaces: an actor in the middle of the street would be erased from the knees down by a rail that is not drawn. Regenerating it at 3700x864 against the current plate is art, and Tyler's.

occlusion.planesNote: AUTHORED HERE, NOT HAND-EDITED IN THE ROOM FILE. Occlusion planes are geometry read off the plate, which is the annotator's whole subject, and a room file the compiler rewrites is not a place a hand edit survives. The compiler emits these; where an annotation declares none it preserves whatever the room already had, so a room converted later loses nothing.

walkBoxesExtraNote: Errata 300 (Tyler, 2026-11-13: "Thad can walk partway up the side of a building. And he just randomly walks up the edge of the porch instead of going up the stairs. On every building."). The street as redrawn has a porch to each building at its own depth, with its own stairs and gaps between, and the old floor ran one boardwalk strip the width of the street across all of it. Now he walks on the ground only: the street from y666 down, and in front of each building a strip up to the foot of what stands there -- the porch's posts, the foot of its stairs, the notice board's legs, the barrels -- each read off the plate. The doors are reached from the street at the foot of their stairs, as every exit's stand already was.
porchesNote: Errata 301 (Tyler, 2026-11-13: "I would like him to actually walk up steps onto porches."). Each porch is a deck, read off the plate from the wall's foot to the deck's front edge, joined to the street only by its stairs, from the deck's edge to the stairs' foot. Nothing else touches a deck, so the only way up is the steps. Deck and stairs are drawn at the height of the ground at the stairs' foot (fixedAt), since a man on a porch is that far away, raised. Each door's stand is on its porch, in front of it.

occluders.note: Errata 302 (Tyler, 2026-11-13: "make sure Thad isn't walking in front of posts on the porch when he should be walking behind them"). Every porch post on the street, read off the plate at 3x: its column from the roof beam to its foot, and the row its foot stands on. A man whose feet are above that row is behind the post and it is cut out of him; at or below it he is in front. The Nugget's posts stand twenty pixels back from the deck's edge and the hotel's at three depths, which is why it is per post and not per box. The Company's and the assay office's columns are pilasters on their walls, and nobody stands behind those. The hotel's two left-hand posts stand at the back of its deck, behind anyone who can stand on it, and are not listed.
